intended_object: The open set of lower-triangular real p×p matrices with strictly positive diagonal, written in the lower-triangle coordinates (one coordinate per entry (i,j) with j ≤ i). This is the parameter domain of Cholesky factors. Inferred from the docstring.
explanation:
`lowerTriangle p` is `{ij : Fin p × Fin p // ij.2 ≤ ij.1}`, so a point `x : lowerTriangle p → ℝ` lists the entries of a lower-triangular matrix. The set asks that every diagonal coordinate `x ⟨(i,i), _⟩` be strictly positive and puts no condition on the entries below the diagonal. So it is exactly the set of Cholesky factors written in these coordinates, as the docstring says.

Degenerate case: for p = 0 the set is the whole (one-point) space. This is correct, since the empty matrix is its own Cholesky factor.

Mathlib has no such coordinate region. The use of real numbers and of `Fin p` comes from the library's coordinate setup for the Lebesgue measure and the Wishart change of variables. Cholesky factors with positive diagonal are standard over ℝ, so this is not too narrow.
